# Listening

Listening involves leaving another person choices. A clean transcript is one useful record, but a question can interrupt someone before they discover what they want to say. A helper at a clinic or a workshop can make a conversation safer by staying nearby, or prevent it by speaking first.

Ask whose decision is being made, who can refuse and what happens after a refusal. Do not infer the reason for silence from the silence itself. Return an account to the person who supplied it and preserve their right to disagree. [[Field methods]] records the distinction between an observation and an interpretation. The old recording examples still matter; I am now trying to understand the conditions that let a person speak without being required to perform gratitude or certainty.
